topic: What sustainable engineering strategies are essential to balance the scalability of LEO satellite constellations with the urgent need to address orbital debris accumulation?
consensus_response: To balance the scalability of LEO satellite constellations with the urgent need to address orbital debris accumulation, we propose a comprehensive strategy that integrates De-Orbiting Satellites with Electrodynamic Tethers (DESET), Orbital Debris Mitigation via In-Orbit Servicing (OIMS), and Satellite-Based Radar Concept (SBRC). DESET generates drag forces to de-orbit satellites, reducing collision risks. OIMS involves deploying robots or drones in LEO to capture and remove existing debris. SBRC uses intersatellite communication signals as radar signals to detect debris objects, eliminating the need for separate spaceborne radar infrastructure. This integration enables a more versatile contingency if some part of the detection system fails, ensuring physical safety in high-density satellite constellations.
reference_context: The reference context highlights the importance of detecting debris objects and their trajectories in LEO satellite constellations, emphasizing the need for advanced signal processing techniques to mitigate interference between satellite signals. It also notes that high-density constellations increase the risk of collisions, necessitating continuous updating of space objects' trajectory models.
